summary.intent: Work through pending todos: wire CTR encryption for media uploads in the SDK, debug BYO-IPFS register-cid 400 errors on staging, and fix the release gate which was failing to detect successful desktop E2E runs.
summary.outcome: Three PRs merged: SDK CTR encryption wiring (#399), BYO-IPFS fix with new PATCH /vault/byo-status endpoint and load test corrections (#400), and release gate rewrite to search desktop-e2e.yml runs directly (#401). Additionally fixed 262 ESLint errors (Rust target/ dir) and initiated GitHub Actions Node.js 24 upgrade.

repo: selectEncryptionMode() existed in streaming-crypto.service.ts for the web app but was never wired into the SDK uploadFile() path — new uploads always used GCM even for large media files that should use CTR.

PATCH /vault/byo-status endpoint did not exist despite setByoStatus() being a service method — BYO mode was dead code with no way to enable it via API, which was the root cause of register-cid 400/403 errors in load tests.
The release gate searched ci-e2e.yml orchestrator runs for desktop E2E results, but successful desktop E2E tests ran as standalone desktop-e2e.yml workflows — the gate never found them.
pnpm api:generate lint step scans target/ (Rust build artifacts), causing 261 spurious ESLint errors from Rust-generated JS files. Fix: add target/** to eslint.config.js ignores.

The todo for 'SDK uploadFile GCM' ended up with both a pending/ and done/ copy on main after the merge of fix/e2e-test-failures-v2 — the branch had committed the done/ copy but main also had the pending/ copy from a different branch.
FLAC files (audio/flac) were missing from STREAMING_MIME_TYPES in both sdk/src/client.ts and apps/web/src/services/streaming-crypto.service.ts.

Pre-existing test errors across API spec files follow a systemic pattern: jest.Mocked<Partial<T>> loses mock method types after module.get(), requiring direct use of the mock object variable rather than the re-fetched module reference.
The load test byo-file-workload.ts was sending { ipnsName, cid } to ipns-publish but PublishIpnsEntryDto requires { ipnsName, record, metadataCid } — the signed IPNS record was never constructed.

code.finding: Centralized STREAMING_MIME_TYPES, CTR_SIZE_THRESHOLD, selectEncryptionMode(), and normalizeEncryptionMode() into a shared module. Both sdk/client.ts and apps/web/src/services/streaming-crypto.service.ts import from here instead of duplicating.
Added optional encryptionMode param; when 'CTR' uses encryptAesCtr + generateCtrIv instead of GCM, passes mode through to createFileMetadata.
uploadFile() now calls selectEncryptionMode(mimeType, size) imported from sdk-core and passes result to sdkCore.uploadFile().
Added PATCH /vault/byo-status endpoint that calls vaultService.setByoStatus(). Previously setByoStatus() existed as a service method but had no controller route.
createByoClientPool now calls PATCH /vault/byo-status on each account after creation and filters out accounts where BYO enable fails; throws if zero accounts succeed.
ipns-publish step replaced bare { ipnsName, cid } call with createAndPublishIpnsRecord from sdk-core to produce a valid signed IPNS record. createSdkContext hoisted outside iteration loop.

Desktop E2E verification rewritten to search desktop-e2e.yml runs directly (not ci-e2e.yml orchestrator). Walks commits newest-first using git log, looks up runs by SHA to ensure commit order matches, polls in-progress runs.
Pattern fix: use mock object variables directly (mockRepublishService, mockTeeKeyStateService) instead of re-fetching via module.get() which loses jest.Mocked<Partial<T>> typing.
Added target/** to ignores — was only excluding src-tauri/target/** but not root target/ which contains Rust build artifacts and doc JS files.

Bare vi.mock('@cipherbox/sdk-core', () => ({ ... })) factory drops all exports not explicitly listed. Fixed by switching to importOriginal + spread so real exports survive alongside mocked functions. Same fix applied to client-extended.test.ts, client.test.ts, bin.test.ts, shared-write.test.ts.

workflow: When centralizing a utility (like selectEncryptionMode), create it in the lowest-level package (sdk-core) and have higher-level packages import from there rather than duplicating.
pnpm api:generate must be run after adding new API endpoints to regenerate the api-client package — missing this causes CI drift checks to fail.

When orval regenerates api-client, all files in packages/api-client/src/ must be committed including newly created model files and generated directories; staging only specific files misses new additions.
For NestJS API spec generation, the API server must be running to generate the OpenAPI spec — the generation script reflects live endpoints.

Entire CLI overwrites .husky/commit-msg locally; add it to .git/info/exclude so local modifications don't pollute git status. The commit-msg.pre-entire (original commitlint hook) should also be excluded.

GitHub Actions node deprecation warnings are silenced by bumping to latest major versions: actions/checkout@v4→v4.2.2 only gets Node24 opt-in, but actions/setup-node@v4→v6 and cache/upload/download-artifact v3→v4 cover most of them. pnpm/action-setup@v4→v5 also needed.

friction: Todo for completed SDK GCM work appeared as both pending/ and done/ on main after merge — required manual cleanup.
pnpm api:generate requires the local API server to be running to generate the OpenAPI spec, making it environment-dependent.
API client drift check in CI failed because regenerated model files were not fully staged — only specific known files were added instead of the full src/ directory.
GraphQL API calls for PR review thread fetching timed out intermittently, requiring fallback to REST API.
Background task notifications for commands that were already resolved in the main conversation created confusion about whether additional action was needed.
Accidentally created apps/api/openapi.json (wrong location) during manual OpenAPI generation — needed a cleanup commit.
Pre-existing test errors across 9+ API spec files (jest.Mocked<Partial<T>> pattern) were blocking typecheck on a branch unrelated to those files.
The release gate failure root cause required inspecting three different workflow run IDs and comparing SHAs before the dual-workflow-type issue became clear.
